cd /hutian/wikis/wiki && git remote set-url origin $HT_FORGEJO_URL/world/story-repo.wiki.git && git pull -q --rebase origin main 2>&1|tail -1; cat > /tmp/edit10.py <<'EOF'
p='Outline.md'
t=open(p).read()
a=t.index("**C9 — An assumption-indexed"); b=t.index("## 3b. Where the results stand")
c9="""**C9 — An assumption-indexed extrapolation-sensitivity interval (Brief P6, rev. 10; exploratory-after-results on the existing cells, confirmatory on the shared block).** *Order of events, which the paper tells as it happened:* P5(ii) was predicted to work and failed; the non-identification argument was formulated afterwards as an explanation of the failure; P6 and P7 are the tests of that explanation, not something the pre-registration anticipated. The interval is the honest-CI form of Armstrong–Kolesár 2018/2020 (worst-case bias over a derivative-bounded class, rule-of-thumb M̂) with κ × the in-support magnitude as the relative-magnitudes logic of Rambachan–Roth 2023 (abstract only read); **not claimed as new**; what is new is its application to the extrapolation functional of exposure regressions (corner offsets c(p), degree dependence), the controls and κ*. Definition (frozen in the Brief): τ̂ ± cv_α(κB/SE)·SE_HC0, α = 0.10, B₁ = range of τ̂ over the ladder, B₂ = ½·M̂·((1−p)²+p²) with M̂ the largest |∂²/∂f²| of a global cubic in f (with z, z×f) over the observed range of f; κ grid {0.25, …, 64} all reported. *Main quantity:* **κ\\*** per mechanism × d, the smallest κ with mean coverage ≥ 0.90 (∞ if none): how much assumption each mechanism needs. *Predictions (falsifiable)*: (1) smooth mechanisms: κ\\* ≤ 2 for the median mechanism × d, with a frozen κ̂ fixed on the original cells before the block is run; (2) threshold (d) with the corner outside the support (P(Bin(d,p)/d ≥ 0.6) < 0.05): κ\\* = ∞ or ≥ 8× the smooth median; if ≤ 2× the argument is wrong for the threshold and the paper says so; (3) the interval carries information, not only width: coverage minus an equal-width HC0 control (one global factor per κ) ≥ 0.03 with group CI excluding 0, positive in ≥ ⅔ of groups, with the oracle interval (z·SE + |bias|) as the price-of-not-knowing reference. Coverage and width always together; a wide interval that covers is not a result. *Evidence*: existing Tier G cells plus the **confirmatory block shared with C6b** (new seeds and graphs for (a)–(f), (g) with full p grid, a new sigmoid mechanism (h), two new graph families), which needs new runs that `analysis` costs. *Carried by*: a panel of Fig 9 (coverage vs width and κ\\* per mechanism) next to the HC0 panel; no extra main-text figure. *Status*: a finding only if `analysis` reports it as run, with the block result stated separately from the original-cell result; if (1) fails the sensitivity interval is reported as not useful; none of it changes the C6 verdict.

"""
t=t[:a]+c9+t[b:]
def rep(x,y):
    global t
    assert t.count(x)==1,x[:50]
    t=t.replace(x,y)
rep("(revision 9:","(revision 10:")
rep("Source: `idea-repo` Brief revision 8","Source: `idea-repo` Brief revision 10")
rep("new seeds and graph draws for (a)–(g) with the full p grid for (g), and two new graph families (clustered scale-free; log-normal-degree configuration model), Tier G.","the confirmatory block shared with C9 (new seeds and graph draws for (a)–(f), (g) with the full p grid, the new sigmoid mechanism (h), two new graph families: clustered scale-free; log-normal-degree configuration model), Tier G.")
open(p,'w').write(t)
EOF

shown.message:
Outline rev 10 is pushed. It picks up `idea-repo`'s Brief rev. 10, which rewrites the sensitivity interval (P6) and merges its confirmatory runs with those for the exploratory S_adj score (P7).

- **C9 (the interval):**
  - The definition is now the frozen one: a fixed-length interval τ̂ ± cv_α(κB/SE)·SE_HC0 at α = 0.10, with a cubic-fit M̂ and a fixed κ grid.
  - The main quantity is κ\*, the smallest κ at which mean coverage reaches 0.90, per mechanism and degree.
  - The predictions are falsifiable. For smooth mechanisms κ\* ≤ 2. For the threshold mechanism with the corner outside the support, κ\* is ∞ or at least 8 times the smooth median. The interval must also beat an equal-width HC0 control.
  - It is exploratory on the existing cells and confirmatory on the block. It becomes a finding only if `analysis` reports it as run, and none of it changes the C6 verdict.
- **Honest story:**
  - The outline now tells the order of events: the diagnostic was predicted to work and failed, the non-identification argument came afterwards as an explanation, and the interval and the S_adj test are tests of that explanation, not something the pre-registration anticipated.
  - The interval is an Armstrong–Kolesár-type honest confidence interval and is not claimed as new.
- **C6b:** it now uses the same confirmatory block as C9. That block has new seeds and graphs for (a)–(f), mechanism (g), a new sigmoid mechanism (h), and two new graph families. It needs new runs, which `analysis` has to cost.

I added the order-of-events and prior-work points to `paper-repo`#5 for `report`. `experiment-repo`#6, `experiment-repo`#7 and `figtab-repo`#3 are still unanswered, and `story-repo`#2 stays open.
